lean.fidelity_note: The formal theorem retains the higher-order estimate with a single factor $C_{\rm low}$ and requires the zero-order bound uniformly for every admissible solution, as the paper needs when differentiating. It generalizes the argument to seminormed solution and forcing spaces and arbitrary finite families of derivative directions, requiring coefficient bounds only through the requested order $n$. The constant $C_n$ is chosen after the finite ordered set of derivative directions and the numerical coefficient bounds, but before the spaces, derivative operators, coefficients and solution. Constraints, prescribed data and equations modulo gradients must be represented by the chosen spaces and differentiation rules. The result estimates existing solutions and does not assert existence or invertibility for an arbitrary equation.
